parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/app.module.ts is the root NestJS module. The layer model puts *.module.ts files in the presentation layer, and their job is to assemble the app. This file only does that kind of work. It registers configuration loaders with ConfigModule.forRoot, sets up I18nModule with a language header resolver, and imports the feature modules. It has no business rules, no domain logic and no data access. The `infrastructureDatabaseModule` block is the borderline part. It chooses MongooseModule or TypeOrmModule depending on the database config, and passes a dataSourceFactory that creates and starts a TypeORM DataSource. This is still module registration in the root module. The actual database settings come from MongooseConfigService and TypeOrmConfigService in other files, and nothing here queries or maps data. A stricter reviewer could say the DataSource factory belongs in a separate database module in the infrastructure layer. That is a reason to tidy the code, not a misplaced responsibility, given that module files are where this setup lives in this layer model.
